# Write the physics in physical coordinates

[A formula should describe the same field whether one rank or several store it.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

Suppose the initial condition is $u(x,y,z)=1+x+y^2$. It contains no MPI
rank and no local memory offset. An initialization routine should preserve
that fact. The previous example 08 simulated four owners within one
process; this refactor constructs one actual owned field per MPI rank.

## The formula stays small

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="initialize" dedent=4}
```

`domain` describes the complete $16\times8\times2$ grid with unit spacing.
`partition` describes ownership. `u` stores only this rank's values.
`apply` bridges those descriptions by supplying physical coordinates to
the lambda.

At global points $(4,2,0)$ and $(12,6,0)$ the answers must be

$$
\begin{gathered}
u(4,2,0)=9, \\
u(12,6,0)=49.
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-probes}

Those values do not depend on the process grid.

## Who owns the point?

For this tiny demonstration, each rank checks its owned cells and a
collective combines the answer:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="probe" dedent=4}
```

The value reduction alone is not enough. A missing point could yield zero,
and two owners could add values together. Reducing the number of owners
as well requires that each requested point is represented exactly once.

This is an inspectable teaching probe, not an efficient general point-query
service: scanning every cell is unnecessary for large repeated query sets.
The example deliberately exposes the ownership decision and its invariant.

## Repeat the experiment with another decomposition

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

Compare this output with `--launcher=none` and four ranks. The source's
domain and formula stay fixed. Each run should report @eq-probes with
`owners=1`. Those assertions are also part of the ordinary numerical checks.

Next, change the x spacing to one half while retaining the same global
probe indices. The physical x coordinates halve. Predict why the first
value becomes seven rather than nine, and update the reference using
physical coordinates rather than copying the previous expected output.

This lesson initializes a field; it does not evolve a PDE or fill halos.
For those operations continue with [finite-difference heat flow](../../heat/finite-differences/index.qmd).
See the [field factory](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/field/field_factory.hpp)
and [Field API](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/data/grid_field.hpp)
for the underlying public operations.
The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
